convoLines.text: "Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"This matters — Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Sure — Anger's a fire — useful if you cook with it, deadly if you sleep next to it. I cook with mine. Most days."
"Hah. Still on whether you're angry."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? I need you to hear that."
"Good question." "Vito owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Vito's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
«नमस्ते! तुम्हारा नाम क्या है?» "Shit." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«बिल्कुल सही कहा।» They nod back, slowly.
«मैं नहीं भूलूँगा।» A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«धन्यवाद। सच में, धन्यवाद।» (you catch 'धन्यवाद' — thanks) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago. You'd know about that."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us? I mean it."
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"Quick version — Still on what you think happened to us."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Don't waste it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The whole fire was arguing about Hummice last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Loud' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. And I've been walking past…'"
"Lockpick — It sits up. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"This one — Salmonberry. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"My part? I count portions out loud before eating and pretend I'm not choosing sides."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
Emilio has an edge today — something curdled.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind? This isn't new."
"Good question." "You're one of the good ones. Don't make me regret saying that out loud." "That's where we are."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"A month ago I wouldn't have said any of this to you. That's not nothing."
"Well — Still on each other."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
«अरे... तुम्हें हिंदी आती है? नहीं? ...धत्।» (you catch 'नहीं' — no, 'हिंदी' — Hindi) "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«यह सच है।» (you catch 'सच' — truth) They nod back, slowly.
«तुम्हारा बहुत-बहुत शुक्रिया।» (you catch 'शुक्रिया' — thanks) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«तुम अच्छे इंसान हो।» (you catch 'अच्छे' — good) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «तुम्हारे पास खाना है?» (Do you have food? — you're fairly sure)
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
«¿Qué lugar es este? ¿Dónde estamos?»
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up? Easy."
«Sí, sí, exacto.» (you catch 'Sí' — yes) They nod back, slowly.
«Eres buena persona.» (you catch 'buena' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Eres un sol, gracias de corazón.» (you catch 'sol' — sun, 'corazón' — heart) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic. "Water?"
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «¿Tú eres... el jefe?» (you catch 'jefe' — boss)
Fernanda lights up. "No, no — like this." They say it slowly, twice, watching your mouth shape it. "Sí, sí, exacto.." You try again. Closer. They grin like you just scored the winning point.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas?» (Hello! What's your name? — you're fairly sure)
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
«Es verdad.» (It's true. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly. "Hello?"
«No lo olvidaré.» (I won't forget it. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Gracias. De verdad, gracias.» (Thanks. Truly, thanks. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «¿Cuántos días llevamos aquí?» (How many days have we been here? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday. Makes sense to me."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"I was an ER nurse — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"Still on what you did for fun. Worth considering."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? One step at a time."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Hardened Gauntlet. They just... took Sofia. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
"Same as always: we endure."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d5: 🕯️ Vito Rios is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d6: That night, they bring Vito home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d7: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d7: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d7: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 37. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d7: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d7: SYSTEM: Quest protocol integrated. Objectives will appear.
d7: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
burialWindowSay: d6: That night, they bring Vito home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d7: 📻 "Why do the small humans keep putting organic matter in their FACE-HOLES? We built you a fusion pellet! ...You BURIED it. WHY did you bury the pellet?!"
d8: You say a few words for them. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d8: You bury them. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d8: "Good question." "Vito owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d8: "Nobody says Vito's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
echoV2Sample: d8: The village raises a marker by the fire — Vito, day 8. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
